boundaries.note: This separate derived layer tests comparison vocabulary. It does not modify or reinterpret accepted evidence records.

statusVocabulary.claimed: An accepted publisher-attributed claim directly supports the attribute across the record scope without choosing among documented alternatives.
statusVocabulary.conditional: An accepted publisher-attributed claim supports the attribute only for a named configuration, release line, path, offering or other explicit scope.
statusVocabulary.explicit-limitation: An accepted publisher-attributed source explicitly limits or excludes the attribute in the mapped scope; this is not an independent finding.
statusVocabulary.unknown: The accepted evidence does not determine the attribute. Unknown is not evidence that the product lacks it.
statusVocabulary.unresolved: Accepted evidence relevant to the attribute cannot yet be reconciled to the exact record scope.
statusVocabulary.not-applicable: The taxonomy definition excludes this record's comparison frame. This status is assigned by the taxonomy rule, not by product inference.

comparisonFrames.label: Interactive CLI
comparisonFrames.description: A user-directed command-line surface whose primary accepted record is local or hybrid rather than a repository-native hosted task.

comparisonFrames.label: Interactive IDE or desktop
comparisonFrames.description: A foreground editor, extension or desktop-agent surface. Related cloud or external-agent surfaces do not inherit its claims.

comparisonFrames.label: Hosted or background service
comparisonFrames.description: A publisher-hosted task or session surface not defined primarily by native repository-service output controls.

comparisonFrames.label: Repository-integrated service
comparisonFrames.description: A hosted or runner-executed surface with native repository authorization, branch, merge-request or pull-request controls.

calculation.configuredClaimedCoverage: (count(status == 'claimed') + count(conditional attributes whose cited scope matches the selected configuration)) / applicableCount
warnings: The unconfigured floor gives no credit to conditional claims.
The documented ceiling is not necessarily achievable because conditional claims can depend on mutually exclusive alternatives.
Evidence completeness measures admitted documentation coverage, not capability, quality or truth.
No metric mixes independent evidence with publisher claims and no current record has an admitted independent test.
Cross-frame ordering is invalid; even within a frame, results remain sensitive to publisher documentation breadth.

attributes.label: Read or inspect workspace files
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly says the mapped surface can read, inspect or explore files or code in its workspace or repository.

attributes.label: Create or modify workspace files
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly says the mapped surface can create, edit, delete or otherwise change workspace or repository files.

attributes.label: Execute terminal or command-line actions
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes terminal, shell or command execution by the mapped surface; a setup system merely existing is insufficient.

attributes.label: Use a browser, fetch or web-oriented tool
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes web browsing, fetch, Playwright, computer use or application testing through a browser-like tool.

attributes.label: Use MCP, connectors or named external tools
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes MCP, connectors or another named external-tool integration available to the mapped surface.

attributes.label: Select or configure a model or provider route
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes user, administrator or configuration selection of a model, provider, gateway or routing mode.

attributes.label: Use a non-writing analysis or plan stage
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly distinguishes a planning or analysis stage that precedes or excludes implementation changes; a mode named Plan without that boundary is insufficient.

attributes.label: Run a hosted, background or asynchronous task
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes a task, session or conversation that executes remotely or in the background rather than only as a foreground local interaction.

attributes.label: Run parallel, spawned or child work
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes parallel tasks, child sessions, subagents or spawned work associated with the mapped surface.

attributes.label: Execute automated tests, linters or app checks
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly says the mapped surface can run automated tests, linters, browser app testing or a named QA workflow.

attributes.label: Delegate between local and remote execution paths
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly distinguishes a local or foreground path from a selectable cloud, hosted, remote-SSH or equivalent execution path without transferring claims between surfaces.

attributes.label: Configure task environment bootstrap
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes setup scripts, snapshots, images, caches or other task-environment bootstrap controls.

attributes.label: Publish a branch through a native hosted workflow
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes native branch publication by the hosted or repository-integrated surface, not merely the possibility of running Git commands.

attributes.label: Create a pull or merge request through the native workflow
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes the mapped hosted surface creating or publishing a pull request or merge request.

attributes.label: Read or respond to pull-request review feedback
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes the mapped hosted surface reading, responding to or implementing pull-request or merge-request feedback.

attributes.label: Human confirmation before individual actions
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes a human confirmation path before individual actions or tool calls. Plan and final-output approvals are separate attributes.

attributes.label: Automatic approval or approval bypass
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes an automatic allow, no-prompt, autonomous or approval-bypass path for actions or tools.

attributes.label: Human approval before plan implementation
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes a human decision that gates movement from a proposed plan to implementation.

attributes.label: Human approval before applying or publishing completed output
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes a post-execution human decision to apply, dismiss or publish completed hosted-task output.

attributes.label: Configure tool availability or allow/deny rules
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes tool-specific availability, enable/disable, allow, deny or confirmation rules rather than only a global execution mode.

attributes.label: Select or rely on a documented sandbox or isolated environment
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes sandboxing, operating-system restrictions, a fresh isolated machine or an isolated background-task environment.

attributes.label: Configure or apply outbound-network restrictions
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes network denial, allowlists, firewall, proxy policy or sandbox egress boundaries.

attributes.label: Restrict repository authorization scope
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes authorization to selected repositories, one repository, all repositories or an equivalent project-access boundary.

attributes.label: Configure scoped credentials, API keys or secrets
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes credential, API-key or secret availability with a named scope, storage path or role boundary.

attributes.label: Identify or select the execution principal
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly identifies service-user, impersonated-user, token, composite-identity, commit-attribution or equivalent execution-principal alternatives.

attributes.label: Select a hosted runner, placement or deployment environment
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes choosing or inheriting a hosted runner, outpost, platform, deployment or other hosted execution placement.

attributes.label: Authorize scheduled or event-triggered invocation
attributes.definition: The publisher explicitly describes scheduled execution, repository-event invocation, mention-based invocation or another non-interactive hosted trigger.
